lenard-1902.title: Ueber die lichtelektrische Wirkung
lenard-1902.note: Measurements showing that the energy of electrons freed by light depends on the light's colour, not its intensity.

prsa-2016.authors: Prša, A.; Harmanec, P.; Torres, G.; Mamajek, E.; Asplund, M.; et al.
prsa-2016.title: Nominal values for selected solar and planetary quantities: IAU 2015 Resolution B3
prsa-2016.note: Defines the nominal solar effective temperature, 5772 K, used for the blackbody sun on these pages.

zhang-2020.authors: Zhang, F.; Castaneda, J. F.; Chen, S.; Wu, W.; DiNezza, M. J.; et al.
zhang-2020.title: Comparative studies of optoelectrical properties of prominent PV materials: Halide perovskite, CdTe, and GaAs
zhang-2020.note: Room-temperature band gaps: GaAs about 1.42 eV, single-crystal CdTe about 1.51 eV, MAPbI3 about 1.61–1.63 eV (arXiv:1907.03434).

doe-cigs.title: Copper indium gallium diselenide
doe-cigs.note: CuInSe2 band gap about 1.04 eV, CuGaSe2 about 1.68 eV; the best devices use a partial substitution of Ga for In. Page first published 24 January 2014 by the Solar Energy Technologies Office and last modified 29 September 2025; the old /eere/solar/ address now leads here (Integrated Energy Systems Office).

street-1991.title: Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon
street-1991.container: Cambridge University Press (Cambridge Solid State Science Series)
street-1991.note: Standard monograph on a-Si:H, including its optical gap of about 1.7 eV and the absence of a sharp band edge.

de-vos-1980.title: Detailed balance limit of the efficiency of tandem solar cells
de-vos-1980.container: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics 13(5), 839–846
de-vos-1980.note: Unconcentrated sunlight: about 30 % for one cell, 42 % for two, 49 % for three, 68 % for an infinite stack; 40 %, 55 %, 63 % and 86 % at maximum concentration.

polman-2016.authors: Polman, A.; Knight, M. W.; Garnett, E. C.; Ehrler, B.; Sinke, W. C.
polman-2016.title: Photovoltaic materials: Present efficiencies and future challenges
polman-2016.note: Compares 16 photovoltaic materials against their Shockley–Queisser detailed-balance limits.

pveducation-si-optical.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-si-optical.title: Optical properties of silicon (PVEducation)
pveducation-si-optical.note: Silicon is an indirect band gap semiconductor with a long, weak absorption tail near the band edge; tabulated absorption coefficients.

pveducation-absorption-depth.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-absorption-depth.title: Absorption depth (PVEducation)
pveducation-absorption-depth.note: In silicon, blue light is absorbed within a few microns while red light needs a few hundred microns.

pveducation-band-gap.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-band-gap.title: Band gap (PVEducation)
pveducation-band-gap.note: The band gap as the minimum energy to free a bound electron into the conduction band, leaving a hole in the valence band.

pveducation-atmosphere.authors: Honsberg, C. B.; Bowden, S. G.
pveducation-atmosphere.title: Atmospheric effects (PVEducation)
pveducation-atmosphere.note: Ozone removes most ultraviolet below 0.3 µm; water vapour and CO2 cut deep troughs in the infrared.
